subject: Hospitality
title: The Labor Cost Crisis
description: A quick win: understand The Labor Cost Crisis.

hook.text: Restaurant labor costs eat 30–35% of revenue—and they're rising. The industry faces a permanent staffing crisis.

buildup.text: Long hours, physical strain, low pay, and no benefits drive high turnover. The average restaurant turns over 75% of staff yearly.

discovery.text: In the U.S., tipped minimum wage can be as low as $2.13/hour. Tips are expected to fill the gap—but they're unpredictable.

twist.text: Some restaurants have eliminated tipping and raised menu prices to pay fair wages. Most guests resist paying 20% more upfront.

climax.text: Post-pandemic labor shortages forced many restaurants to raise wages. The industry is slowly, painfully repricing itself.

punchline.text: Cheap meals require cheap labor. The math is finally catching up.

quiz.question: What is the average annual staff turnover rate in restaurants?
